  <div class="attributed-text-segment-list__container relative mt-1 mb-1.5 babybear:mt-0 babybear:mb-0.5">
    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Network for Learning is deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Dame Karen Poutasi, a distinguished public servant whose leadership and service made a lasting contribution to Aotearoa New Zealand.

Dame Karen was deeply committed to equity, ensuring that New Zealand’s systems enabled opportunity and progress that were not shaped by circumstance. She led with integrity, fairness and a steadfast focus on long-term outcomes, doing the right thing, even when difficult. Always with a keen eye on the future while respecting the past, she championed progress that delivers real impact for all learners. While she is rightly recognised for her transformative leadership in health, her contribution to education was equally significant.

As a relatively young organisation, we have many people who are growing into new leadership roles and stepping up through the ranks. Dame Karen took genuine interest in our people and was always generous with her time. She treated everyone with respect, made space for every voice, and had a unique ability to empower and support others to be their best. Her encouragement and belief in people will long be remembered across N4L.

As Deputy Chair of Network for Learning, Dame Karen played a pivotal role in strengthening the accessibility and resilience of digital infrastructure across our education system. Her leadership helped ensure all schools and kura, and their ākonga, have equal access to high-quality, secure and safer internet connectivity in ways that do not depend on location or personal circumstances. Her work supported learners across the motu to thrive in an increasingly digital world.

In recognition of her significant services to education and the state, Dame Karen was appointed a Dame Companion of the New Zealand Order of Merit in 2020. Her legacy is one of principled leadership grounded in equity and the long-term public good, and a deep commitment to building trusted systems that serve all learners and communities.

At N4L, we honour her belief in strong, trusted systems and her enduring commitment to ensuring all learners, wherever they are, and whatever their circumstances, have the foundations they need to succeed.

We extend our deepest sympathies to Dame Karen’s whānau, friends and colleagues at this very sad time. We are grateful for her leadership, her generosity of spirit, and the example she set for us all. She will be deeply missed.

Haere rā, Dame Karen. Thank you for your extraordinary contribution to education, public service and Aotearoa New Zealand.</p>
